payload.summary: Evaluated all 6 amendments against the codebase. The exploration confirms: (1) concentration helpers each independently recompute water_volume_l() via substrate layer iteration, (2) nitrifier yields are at 0.05/0.04/0.03 with 0.5g carrying capacity, (3) all Monod kinetics use total mass not concentrations, (4) soft_acidic.toml has alkalinity=1.07/DIC=12.0/bicarb=65.3, (5) save.rs hard-rejects schema != 3 with no migration path. All amendments identify real issues — from performance overhead and bundled behavioral changes to physical correctness gaps and save compatibility breakage.

votes.rationale: Valid performance concern. Each TankState concentration helper independently calls water_volume_l() → substrate_depth_cm(), which iterates substrate layers. When snapshot.rs::from_state calls ~12-15 helpers, the volume is recomputed ~12-15 times despite being invariant within the call. While the per-call cost is small (summing a few layer depths + arithmetic), the pattern is wasteful by design. The fix is straightforward: either pass pre-computed volume to the helpers or add a compute-once-and-reuse pattern. Low severity but easy to fix and good for code hygiene.

Bundling 50x growth yield increases (AOB 0.001→0.05, NOB 0.001→0.04, comammox 0.0008→0.03) plus a new logistic carrying capacity (0.5g) in the same changeset as structural concentration helpers is poor changeset hygiene. These parameter changes materially alter cycling dynamics — biofilter maturation will be dramatically faster. If the volume-basis refactor introduces a regression in nitrogen cycling behavior, it will be impossible to distinguish from the intended behavioral change caused by the yield adjustment. These should be separate commits/changesets so each can be evaluated and reverted independently.

The doc comments currently say things like 'Half-saturation for DOC (mg C total)' which is accurate but misleading. Monod K_s constants are physically concentration-dependent quantities — a 5mg total half-saturation means different effective concentrations in a 10L vs 100L tank. Since this is explicitly deferred to tanksim-6e5.2.3, adding a brief note like 'Interim total-mass parameterization; see tanksim-6e5.2.3 for conversion to concentration-based K_s' costs almost nothing and prevents future contributors from assuming these are proper concentration-based constants. The current docs are technically accurate but create a subtle trap.

Doubling alkalinity (0.535→1.07 meq/L), DIC (6→12 mg/L), and bicarbonate (32.6→65.3 mg/L) in the soft_acidic preset is a significant data change that affects any scenario using this water profile. The description says 'KH ~3.0' which at 1.07 meq/L is correct (1.07 meq/L ≈ 3 dKH), suggesting the old values at 0.535 meq/L (~1.5 dKH) were wrong. But if this correction is related to the volume-basis fix (old code computed concentrations against gross volume, inflating apparent concentrations from lower totals), that rationale must be documented. Bundling undocumented data corrections with a structural refactor makes it impossible to verify correctness.

This is the most significant correctness issue. The codebase exploration confirms: nitrogen_cycle.rs uses raw doc_total/don_total for Monod kinetics, algae_growth.rs uses raw ammonia_total+nitrate_total for nutrient limitation, and plant_growth.rs uses raw DIC/N/P totals for half-saturation. All k_* constants are parameterized in total mass. This means two tanks with identical concentrations but different water volumes produce different biological rates — a 10L tank and a 100L tank with the same mg/L concentrations will have fundamentally different nitrogen cycling, algae growth, and plant growth dynamics. The new concentration helpers exist but aren't used where they matter most. The helper layer is decoration, not the canonical source of truth, until it's actually wired into the kinetics.

Hard-rejecting all schema 2 saves with no migration path is a severe user-facing regression. The save.rs code (lines 40-49) returns SchemaVersionMismatch for any schema != 3, and this is test-verified. Meanwhile, WaterState::rescale_totals_for_volume() (water.rs:179-202) already provides the mechanism to adjust chemistry totals when volume basis changes — exactly what a schema 2→3 migration would need. The geometry helpers for computing net volume are also available. A migration function that loads schema 2 data, computes the old gross volume and new net volume, calls rescale_totals_for_volume, and bumps the schema version would preserve user saves. Permanently breaking save compatibility for a units refactor, when the migration tools exist, is unnecessarily destructive.
